## First yearbook delivery -- sources FAO & OLADE (Sept)

### FAO

All of the processing code related for FAO data can be found in the file `fao.R`. 


### OLADE

There are three files associated with the processing of the OLADE energy data: `manual_olade.qmd`, `format_olade.qmd` and `olade.R`. 

The first step is to follow the instructions in the file `manual_olade.qmd` to manually download the necessary raw files. You will need to create an account with OLADE to download the 6 tables detailed in the instructions. Download and save the files locally as described.

Next, run the script `format_olade.R` to take the raw OLADE files and transform them into standard, long data tables.

Finally, source the script `olade.R` to get the indicator-specific cleaning functions. Process the indicators via the `run_all.R` driver.

Quality check them, upload them to Wasabi, and assess their metadata like usual.

# Claude version
# Annual Update Guide

This guide walks through running a full annual update of CEPALSTAT's environmental indicators, start to finish.
It's written for someone with limited R experience and no prior exposure to this repository — if you can follow
along and get through one full cycle, you'll understand how the pieces connect. For the bigger-picture explanation
of *why* each stage exists and how the scripts are organized, see **[README.md](README.md)**; this guide is the
step-by-step companion to it.

> ✏️ **Note to reviewer (Alexis):** sections marked with ✏️ need repo- or org-specific detail filled in
> (login links, package install sources, credential locations) before this goes out for training — I don't have
> that operational information to fill in accurately.

## When to use this guide

Once a year, when a new year of data becomes available from each source. This is about **refreshing existing
indicators with a new year of data** — it does not cover adding a brand-new indicator to the pipeline (that
involves writing a new `indicator_spec()`, which is a separate, more involved task).

## Before you start

### Software and access checklist

- [ ] R and RStudio installed
- [ ] This repository cloned locally, opened via `cepalstat-data-upload.Rproj`
- [ ] Required R packages installed — see the `library()` calls at the top of `Scripts/utils.R` for the full list
      (tidyverse, magrittr, readxl, writexl, httr2, jsonlite, glue, here, assertthat, quarto, memoise, beepr,
      pdftools, `CepalStatR`, `FAOSTAT`, `fishstat`)
  - ✏️ *Alexis: note here where `CepalStatR`/`fishstat` install from if not CRAN (e.g. a GitHub remote / internal
    package source), and any access token needed.*
- [ ] An account on each manual-download source: EM-DAT, IRENA, IAF/ISO Survey, UNEP, Ramsar (see
      `Scripts/download_other.qmd` for account creation links)
- [ ] ✏️ *Wasabi login — link and where credentials live*
- [ ] ✏️ *CEPALSTAT Admin login — link and where credentials live*
- [ ] Only needed for the optional metadata phase: an `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` added to your `.Renviron` file
      (`usethis::edit_r_environ()` opens it)

### Local folders

`Data/Raw/`, `Data/Cleaned/`, and `Data/Checks/` are not stored in git — they're created and filled locally as
you work. If they don't exist yet under `Data/`, create them (with a subfolder per source under `Raw/`, e.g.
`Data/Raw/climate watch/`, `Data/Raw/olade/`, `Data/Raw/emdat/`, `Data/Raw/fao/`, `Data/Raw/other/`).

### A few R conventions used throughout this repo

You don't need to be an R expert to run the annual update, but these patterns show up constantly:

- **`source(here("Scripts/utils.R"))`** at the top of a script loads shared functions from another file — you'll
  see this in nearly every script.
- **The pipe, `%>%`** — reads as "then." `data %>% filter(x) %>% summarize(y)` means "take `data`, then filter it,
  then summarize it."
- **`spec_<indicator_id>`** — each indicator has a "spec" object (built with `indicator_spec()`) bundling
  everything needed to clean it: its raw data, its max year, how to filter/transform it, etc. You won't need to
  write new ones for an annual update, but you will edit a couple of values inside existing ones (Phase 2 below).

## The annual cycle at a glance

1. Download this year's raw data from each source
2. Update the "max year" in each cleaning script
3. Run the cleaning pipeline
4. Review each indicator in the QC dashboard
5. Upload validated files to Wasabi
6. *(Optional)* Refresh indicator metadata

---

## Phase 1: Download this year's raw data

Downloading works differently per source. Follow the instructions for each:

| Source | How | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Climate Watch | Run `Scripts/download_climatewatch.R` | Saves automatically |
| InforMEA | Run `Scripts/download_informea.qmd` | Saves automatically |
| FAOSTAT / FishStat / Aquastat | Run `Scripts/fao.R`'s download section | Saves automatically |
| OLADE | Follow `Scripts/download_olade.qmd` | Manual — multiple files |
| EM-DAT, IRENA, IAF/ISO Survey, UNEP, Ramsar | Follow `Scripts/download_other.qmd` (one section per source) | Manual — save to the exact filename each section specifies |

For the manual sources, `download_other.qmd` and `download_olade.qmd` spell out exactly which filters to select
on each provider's website and what to name the saved file. Getting the filename right matters — the cleaning
scripts look for that exact pattern.

## Phase 2: Point the pipeline at the new year

Each source's cleaning script defines its own "max year" constant near the top of the file — this is what tells
`process_indicator()` how far to trust the new data. Update each one before running the pipeline:

| Script | Constant |
|---|---|
| `climatewatch.R` | `max_year_cw` |
| `emdat.R` | `max_year_emdat` |
| `fao.R` | `max_year_fao` |
| `olade.R` | `max_year_olade` |
| `other.R` | `max_year_other` |

For example, in `climatewatch.R`:

```r
max_year_cw <- 2023 # as of July 2026
```

Change the year (and update the comment) to reflect the latest year with complete data from that source — this
isn't always the current calendar year, since sources publish on their own schedules. If a source's data is
incomplete for its most recent year (see the code comments near each constant for known caveats), use the last
*complete* year instead.

## Phase 3: Run the cleaning pipeline

`Scripts/run_all.R` is the entry point. Open it and work through it top to bottom:

1. It sources every cleaning script (`utils.R`, `process_indicator_fn.R`, `fao.R`, `olade.R`, `emdat.R`,
   `climatewatch.R`, `other.R`) — this reads in this year's raw data and (re)defines every indicator's spec.
2. `global_spec` controls two things:
   - `diagnostics = TRUE` prints a comparison summary against currently published data — leave this on.
   - `export` — leave `FALSE` for an initial test run (nothing is written to disk yet); set `TRUE` once you're
     ready to actually produce files for QC review and upload.
3. Define `run_list` — the indicator IDs you want to process. You can filter the metadata table
   (`meta %>% filter(source == "...") %>% pull(id)`) to run a whole source at once, or list specific IDs.
4. Run `run_many_indicators(run_list)` to process them all, or `run_one_indicator(id)` for a single one.

Watch the console output as it runs:

- `✅` messages mean that step succeeded.
- `⚠️` messages are worth reading but don't stop execution — e.g. "Source changed" or "Footnotes changed" — they
  flag something to double-check in Phase 4, not necessarily a problem.
- `❌` means something failed validation (see **Troubleshooting** below) — that indicator was not processed and
  needs to be fixed before moving on.

With `export = TRUE`, each successfully processed indicator writes two files:

- `Data/Cleaned/id{indicator_id}_{timestamp}.xlsx` — the final file that will eventually go to Wasabi
- `Data/Checks/comp_id{indicator_id}.xlsx` — the comparison file the QC dashboard reads next

## Phase 4: QC review in the dashboard

Open `Scripts/dashboard/dashboard.qmd` and run it (in RStudio, click **Run Document**). Enter an indicator ID to
review.

The dashboard compares the newly cleaned data against what's currently published on CEPALSTAT and flags:

- **Value differences** — entries where the new value differs from the published value by more than 20%
- **Statistical outliers** — entries flagged by a z-score threshold
- **New / missing entries** — data points present in one version but not the other

Use the sidebar filters (Country, plus one per additional dimension) and the Inspect Country view to dig into any
flag. A flag isn't automatically wrong — it might be a real, expected change (e.g. a source revised historical
values) — but it needs a human decision either way. The dashboard's Metadata Check page also compares this
indicator's assigned source and footnotes against what's currently published.

**If something looks wrong:** go back to the relevant cleaning script, adjust that indicator's spec (e.g. its
`filter_data` or `transform_data` function), and re-run Phase 3 for that indicator. Only touch
`Scripts/process_indicator_fn.R` or `Scripts/utils.R` if the issue is genuinely shared across every indicator —
it isn't the first place to look.

**Once it looks right:** that indicator is ready for upload.

## Phase 6 (optional): Refresh indicator metadata

This step is independent of the data refresh above and doesn't need to happen every year for every indicator —
use it when an indicator's written definition/methodology is stale.

`Scripts/run_meta.R` walks through the workflow, using functions from `Scripts/technical_sheet.R`:

1. Pick one indicator from a group as the **pilot**, and run `suggest_metadata_en()` on it — this drafts English
   metadata using AI assistance, saved to `Metadata/Outputs/`.
2. **Review and edit the draft by hand.** This is a required checkpoint, not optional — the draft is a starting
   point.
3. Run `translate_metadata_es()`, then `export_metadata_admin()` to produce a CEPALSTAT Admin-ready import file.
4. Manually publish the pilot indicator's metadata in CEPALSTAT Admin.
5. Loop the same steps (`suggest_metadata_en()`, review, `translate_metadata_es()`, `export_metadata_admin()`)
   over the rest of the indicator group, using the pilot as the "gold standard" example for consistency.
6. Review the full batch, then publish in CEPALSTAT Admin.

## Troubleshooting

| Message | What it means |
|---|---|
| `❌ NA values found in ...` | A row is missing a value where one is required — usually a raw file formatting change from the source, or a country name that failed to standardize. Check the raw file first. |
| `❌ Duplicate keys found in ...` | The same combination of dimensions (e.g. same country + year) appears more than once — usually a raw file that wasn't filtered/aggregated as expected. |
| `❌ extra columns found: ...` | The cleaned data has a column that doesn't match the indicator's `dim_config` — check the `transform_data` function for that indicator. |
| A cleaning script errors on `read_csv`/`read_xlsx` before anything else runs | The expected raw file isn't where the script is looking, or was saved under a different name — recheck Phase 1. |

If you're stuck beyond this table, the `⚠️`/`❌` messages plus the failing indicator's spec (in its source's
cleaning script) are the fastest way to narrow down what changed.

## Glossary

- **Indicator ID** — CEPALSTAT's numeric identifier for a single indicator (e.g. `2487`).
- **Spec** — an `indicator_spec()` object bundling everything needed to clean one indicator.
- **`dim_config`** — a small table mapping an indicator's data columns (e.g. `Country`, `Years`) to CEPALSTAT's
  internal dimension IDs.
- **Comp file** — the `comp_id{id}.xlsx` file comparing newly cleaned data to currently published data; what the
  QC dashboard reads.
- **LAC** — Latin America and the Caribbean; most indicators include an aggregated regional total for it.
- **Wasabi** — CEPALSTAT's automated data ingestion tool; the final upload destination for cleaned files.
